links.comparator_used: PDA-Alpha (trained at center 1 only) applied as-is at center 2, without adaptation to local data
links.outcome: Positive predictive value and false-positive predictions for pneumothorax detection on the center 2 test set (n=200)
links.effect: PPV rose from 0.525 to 0.886 (p = 0.041). False positives fell from 7 to 1. Sensitivity was unchanged (49/50 for both). AUC was 0.993 for PDA-Alpha and 0.986 for PDA-Beta.
links.tradeoff: Needed 50 locally obtained pneumothorax radiographs. AUC was slightly lower after adaptation (0.986 vs 0.993, overlapping CIs). The optimal amount of local data is still undetermined.
links.quote: The positive predictive value increased from 0.525 to 0.886 after external validation (p = 0.041).

links.comparator_used: PDA-Alpha trained on single-site data (center 1 only)
links.outcome: Positive predictive value and false-positive predictions at the second center after adding data from that center
links.effect: PPV rose from 0.525 to 0.886 (p = 0.041). False positives fell from 7 to 1. Sensitivity was unchanged (49/50). AUC was 0.993 vs 0.986.
links.tradeoff: Only 50 additional radiographs from center 2 were used. AUC was slightly lower (0.986 vs 0.993). The amount of external data needed to fully address generalizability remains unknown.
links.quote: Both algorithms successfully detected the presence of pneumothorax on 49/50 radiographs; however, PDA-Alpha had seven false-positive predictions, whereas PDA-Beta had one.

design_hint: local validation / fine-tuning with local data before deployment
